title: Western Deffufa, Kerma
summary: The Western Deffufa at Kerma in Sudan is a mudbrick temple tower, about 19 m high today after erosion, with a base of roughly 27 by 52 m. Archaeology magazine says it was built some 4,000 years ago and enlarged from a chapel into a multistory temple that became the religious centre of the city.

uncertainty.note: Archaeology magazine, published in 2020, says the temple was constructed some 4,000 years ago. It dates the founding of the city of Kerma to around 2500 B.C. and says a small chapel was built where the Deffufa later stood, without dating the chapel or the enlargement. End is the present: the structure stands.

as_recorded.value: a city that was founded there around 2500 B.C.

when.display: Built c. 4,000 years ago; stands today

where.modern_name: Western Deffufa, Kerma, Northern State, Sudan
where.historical_name: Temple of the Kerma culture (Kingdom of Kerma), Nubia

importance.justification: Archaeology magazine calls it the religious center of Kerma, described as the earliest urban center in Africa outside Egypt.

footprint.description: A solid mudbrick block about 52 m by 27 m at the base (EBSCO Research Starters: 89 by 179 feet).

measurements.note: present-day height about 62 feet (19 meters), reduced by erosion; Archaeology magazine says it looms 65 feet above the site

lod.representation: solid mudbrick block drawn from its published base and height

phases.description: Constructed some 4,000 years ago and enlarged from a chapel into a multistory temple (Archaeology magazine); it stands today at about 19 m, reduced by erosion (EBSCO).

model.no_mesh: Measurements come only from a reference encyclopedia (EBSCO), not a heritage body, museum or scholarly source; kept as data.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the measurements are from EBSCO Research Starters (a reference product, the same class used for the Aswan record) and the height matches Archaeology magazine within a metre; no heritage-body or excavation-report page was opened (UNESCO returned 403). Other pages give 45 x 27 m or 50 x 25 m. Block shape chosen as closest; the start year -1999 is only 4,000 years before the 2020 article, and no page gives a precise date for the chapel or the enlargement.
